checks.name: map_quality_is_measured_on_the_registered_point_set
checks.detail: SA/DA/AA in this stage come from re-scoring the *normalised* maps the registration actually used, not from the as-submitted tables - so the comparison is between two views of one identical point set

findings.name: cannot_reproduce_the_published_number_on_free_data
findings.detail: KISS-ICP's metric is the KITTI devkit one: segments of {100..800} m starting every 10 frames. This trajectory is 108.3 m, so it yields exactly 2 error sample(s). The paper's 0.5 % averages hundreds of samples over the full KITTI sequences (thousands of metres each). 2 samples is a sanity run, not a reproduction.

findings.name: all_four_paper_datasets_are_gated
findings.detail: KITTI odometry needs registration (~80 GB), MulRan needs registration, Boreas needs a form, and Newer College's download page carries no direct links (its download is reported broken upstream). Reproducing the published numbers requires registering for KITTI.

findings.name: kiss_icp_1_3_0_breaks_on_numpy_2
findings.detail: pipeline.py:130 calls float() on a shape-(1,) timestamp array, which NumPy 2 no longer allows. The crash is in the TUM-format writer, which runs after _run_evaluation() - so no metric is affected, but without the one-line patch in work/local_patches.patch the run dies before returning them.

findings.name: no_loop_closure_by_design
findings.detail: there is no loop closure, no pose graph and no keyframe selection - 141 frames, 50 Hz, 20 ms/frame on CPU. Drift is bounded only by ICP itself, which matters for the H1' experiment in 01-01: a 'cleaned map hurts localization' result could be drift rather than map quality.

findings.name: h1_prime_ranking_comparison
findings.detail: at the most discriminating perturbation level (L2), ranking by AA gives dufomap > beautymap > removert_port > removert_official > uncleaned > erasor_port, while ranking by registration failure gives removert_port < dufomap < removert_official < beautymap < uncleaned < erasor_port. Spearman rho(AA, localization utility) = 0.7827 at that level (utility = 100 - failure rate, so positive means the rankings agree), L0: 0.6547, L1: 0.6547, L2: 0.7827, L3: 0.5508; against the *as-submitted* SA/DA/AA the same comparison gives 0.3769 (SA: 0.2319). The task book's H1' predicts rho < 0.9, i.e. that the two rankings differ - it holds even against the kindest pairing. Spread per level: L0: spread 19.9 pp, L1: spread 19.1 pp, L2: spread 17.7 pp, L3: spread 14.2 pp.

findings.name: downstream_numbers_are_self_registration_not_a_revisit
findings.detail: the maps were built from these same 141 frames, so every query's own points are in the map it is registered into. The absolute failure rates are therefore optimistic; what the experiment supports is the *ranking* comparison, because every map is treated identically. A true revisit test needs a second session over the same place.

findings.name: the_official_erasor_map_cannot_enter_this_experiment
findings.detail: the official ERASOR output is expressed in the official bag's SuMa frame, which differs from the benchmark's world frame by ~1.6 m median nearest-neighbour distance (measured in 03_erasor). It fails 100 % of registrations at every perturbation level for that reason, so it is excluded rather than silently scored as a bad map.

reproductions.note: KISS-ICP on a reconstructed 141-frame KITTI 00 sub-sequence: ATE 0.112 m, avg translation error 0.409 % over only 2 metric sample(s) - the paper's 0.5 % is NOT reproduced (see findings). Downstream localizability: rho(normalised AA, utility) = 0.7827 at level L2, rho(as-submitted AA, utility) = 0.3769

checks.name: reproduces_paper_headline

checks.name: gt_is_binary_and_rare_dynamic

checks.name: dp_is_load_bearing
checks.detail: d_p=2 keeps +1.92 pp more static and removes -2.09 pp fewer dynamic points than the paper's d_p=1

findings.name: upstream_example_contradicts_the_paper

The two AA values are 0.09 pp apart while SA and DA each move ~2 pp in opposite directions - the geometric mean of a rare-positive problem is almost entirely SA, so it cannot tell a conservative cleaner from an aggressive one.

findings.name: dynamic_points_are_0_55_percent_of_the_map

reproductions.title: BeautyMap: Binary-Encoded Adaptable Ground Matrix for Dynamic Points Removal in Global Maps
reproductions.heading: 01-06 · BeautyMap
reproductions.verdict: ✅ 能：官方仓库 `python main.py`，配同一套官方评测，命中论文表 I。

checks.name: reproduces_paper_row
checks.detail: SA/DA/HA = 96.95/98.34/97.64 vs BeautyMap Table I p.6 96.76/98.38/97.56, within 0.5 pp

checks.name: aa_and_ha_agree_only_because_sa_da_are_close
checks.detail: AA 97.6431 vs HA 97.6407 - the two means differ by 0.0024 pp here because SA and DA are within 1.4 pp of each other. That is a property of this method on this sequence, not of the metrics.

findings.name: upstream_does_not_run_on_numpy_2
findings.detail: BeautyMap's vendored utils/pcdpy3.py calls np.fromstring (line 150) and ndarray.tostring (line 265), both removed in NumPy 2. Two LOCAL PATCHed lines (frombuffer(...).copy() and tobytes(order='C')) are required. The first failure is at read time; the second only after ~50 s of processing, at write time - a fresh clone that patches only the first looks fine until it has done all the work.

findings.name: matches_the_benchmark_papers_HA_column_too
findings.detail: This run also reproduces the HA column that the BeautyMap paper prints for the other methods: Removert 41.53/58.59 and ERASOR 98.54/79.55 predicted from this paper's Table I, and measured here as 41.5313/58.591 and 98.5352/79.5563. Two papers and four methods now agree on the same numbers, which is the strongest evidence we have that the whole data-and-evaluation chain is right.

findings.name: beautymap_is_the_balanced_one
findings.detail: BeautyMap SA 96.95 / DA 98.34 sits between Removert's refuse-to-delete (99.44/41.53) and ERASOR's delete-too-much (66.71/98.54), and is the only one of the four with both above 96.

reproductions.note: BeautyMap on KITTI 00: SA/DA/HA = 96.95/98.34/97.64 vs paper 96.76/98.38/97.56

findings.name: rotational_rpe_depends_on_an_unspecified_convention
findings.detail: our rotational RPE is 0.604 °/s by RMSE but 0.475 °/s by mean, against the paper's 0.47 °/s. The column is headed only 'RPE rotation (°/s)'. findings.name: cheap_semantics_is_the_actual_contribution
findings.detail: reading the official source, the system DOES use a neural network (YOLO-fastest-xl at 320x320, System.cc:217) - what it removes is the tracker's dependency on waiting for it (Tracking.cc:1592 never blocks, Tracking.cc:4286 propagates the old mask with LK optical flow). So it is a scheduling result, not a geometry-only result, and it inherits COCO's blind spot for unknown dynamic objects.

checks.detail: saveAllTypeOfScans() - the last statement of Removerter::run() - wrote 81 files per directory into scans_nd_strong/ (81), scans_updated/ (81), scans_updated_strong/ (81); the output directory is wiped before the run and the driver removes the completion marker first, so these cannot be a previous run's leftovers

checks.name: change_detection_found_both_directions
checks.detail: nd_map.pcd (central-only) 218931 points, pd_map.pcd (query-only) 43853 points; both empty would mean the two sessions saw identical geometry and nothing was measured

findings.name: coverage_caps_the_comparable_score
findings.detail: only 71.6% of the benchmark's GT static points (12363618 of 17266247) are observed by the 110 input scans this run consumed (92.2% for dynamic). On the full 141-frame GT the same map scores SA 49.51 / DA 76.50, i.e. the sibling rows (removert 99.44 / erasor 66.71 / dufomap 97.96 SA) are not like-for-like: their maps cover all 141 frames. The coverage-matched GT (SA 69.14 / DA 74.51) is the fair partner.

findings.name: the_sa_loss_is_a_deliberate_trade_for_dynamic_rejection
findings.detail: on one identical GT - the central session's own footprint, 11497294 static / 49658 dynamic points, against which all three maps are measured - the no-removal control (the raw central map, 2675552 points) scores SA 99.44 / DA 1.65: it keeps everything and rejects nothing. After the change detection, updated_map.pcd scores SA 69.75 / DA 79.22 and the merged scan-side output SA 64.08 / DA 79.85. So the detector trades 29.7 pp of static preservation for 77.6 pp of dynamic rejection on this pair - aggressive next to 01-04's Removert run on the same kind of data (SA 99.62 / DA 89.25), which is upstream's own configuration difference: 01-04 runs params_kitti.yaml with dist_nn_points_within 0.1, ltremovert's params_ltmapper.yaml asks for 0.01, i.e. a ten times stricter requirement that two sessions agree.

findings.name: the_run_has_two_upstream_outputs_and_they_are_close
findings.detail: on the identical central-session GT, map-side updated_map.pcd scores SA 69.75 / DA 79.22 (758034 points) and the scan-side merged scans_updated/ SA 64.08 / DA 79.85 (7100330 points) - AA 74.33 vs 71.53. Unlike 01-04, where the two outputs of one Removert run sat at opposite corners of the trade-off, here the choice of output moves AA by 2.8 pp; what moves this score is which GT footprint it is measured on (central GT AA 74.33, both-sessions GT AA 71.78, full 141-frame GT AA 61.54).

findings.name: nd_pd_asymmetry_is_the_signature_of_a_partial_overlap
findings.detail: central-only points (nd_map) 218931 vs query-only points (pd_map) 43853 - a 5.0x asymmetry. The query session covers a ~15 m stretch of the central session's 40.8 m trajectory, so far more of the central map is unseen by the query than the other way round. A real multi-session pair (the paper's two visits to one car park) would not have this shape.

findings.name: the_paper_headline_is_not_reachable_from_this_checkout
findings.detail: LT-mapper's delta-map numbers (85.7 MB vs 213.6 MB, 9.8 s vs 87/160 s) belong to the LT-map module, which is absent from the repository: a whole-checkout grep for delta_map/meta_map returns nothing and Removerter.cpp:1671 mentions it only in a comment. Tab. I/II also need MulRan KAIST 04, an extended sequence obtained by e-mail. No run of this checkout can produce those numbers, in any environment.

findings.name: what_change_means_on_this_input
findings.detail: one continuous KITTI 00 pass split at frames 4390..4470 / 4451..4530, not the paper's six sessions over three days. 'Change' here is moving cars plus occlusion and viewpoint differences between two nearby stretches of one drive; the gap between these numbers and the paper's ParkingLot experiment is the experiment, not the implementation.

findings.name: runtime
findings.detail: the official node ran over 81 central + 29 query keyframes in 36 s wall clock (it does all the work in its constructor and then spins; the same input took ~32 s on a cold page cache and ~8 s warm, so read this as seconds, not as a benchmark). This is not the paper's 9.8 s figure: that one times the LT-map delta-map update, whose code is absent here, and it is not comparable to a whole change-detection pass.

findings.name: roi_rule_recomputed_from_the_poses_matches_the_run
findings.detail: work/make_coverage_matched_gt.py recomputes Session.cpp:234's 10 m ROI rule from the two pose files and gets 29 query keyframes, the same number ltremovert logged - so the fair GT's footprint really is the run's input footprint.

findings.name: obb_estimator_versus_repo_renderer
findings.detail: the two observability measurements agree on 22/31 objects (71%); where they differ the repository's renderer is right, because it renders the real mesh while the OBB estimator samples a box surface that includes faces pointing away from the camera

findings.name: vanished_objects_are_not_all_observable
findings.detail: 1 of 1 objects missing from B were NOT observable there (out of view or occluded) — for those the dataset's silence cannot be read as 'removed'

findings.name: observability_spreads_even_within_one_gt_class
findings.detail: unchanged objects: visible=6, occluded=4, out_of_view=13, insufficient=3

findings.name: frame_coverage_is_partial
findings.detail: 51 of 753 frames shipped, a prefix — `out_of_view` is provisional

findings.name: geometric_separation
findings.detail: smallest real motion 0.265 m vs largest alignment noise 0.639 m — moved objects are NOT separable on geometry alone

reproductions.title: ConceptGraphs: Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graphs for Perception and Planning
reproductions.static_status: ⬜ 未开始（论文报告值已记录）
reproductions.heading: 02-03 · ConceptGraphs
reproductions.verdict: ⛔ 本机不能：要 CUDA（PyTorch + PyTorch3D），本机没有 GPU。
reproductions.note: this machine has no GPU (nvidia-smi/nvcc absent, no /usr/local/cuda*); 20-core CPU, 15 GB RAM. ConceptGraphs (ICRA 2024) needs a GPU for SAM (ViT-H) + CLIP + LLaVA-7B; the LVLM alone is ~14 GB in fp16, so 16-24 GB of VRAM is the realistic floor, plus a paid GPT-4 (gpt-4-0613) API key for the LLM stage. Data: Replica / HM3D, public. Recorded in paper_baseline.md, which also lists the paper's own headline numbers, so the target is known before the hardware arrives.
